body.statement: The minimum-weight internal vertex-cut problem on a finite directed or undirected graph with nonnegative vertex weights is solvable in polynomial time by vertex splitting followed by a maximum-flow computation.

source.locator: Definition 7 and the paragraph immediately following it on page 13; vertex-splitting details in Appendix F
source.verbatim_statement: Further, min-weight vertex cut can be reduced to min-weight edge cut through a trivial reduction: We replace every vertex v with two vertices v1, v2, add an edge from v1 to v2 with the same weight as the weight of v in the original graph, and connect every edge that goes into v to v1, and every edge that goes out of v to v2. The resulting problem can be solved using any of the standard max-flow-min-cut algorithms.

upstream.citation: L. R. Ford, Jr. and D. R. Fulkerson. Maximal flow through a network. Canadian Journal of Mathematics 8:399--404, 1956. DOI: 10.4153/CJM-1956-045-5.

attestation.note: Verified against Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash, Optimal Experiment Design for Causal Effect Identification, JMLR 26(28), 2025: Definition 7 and following paragraph on p. 14 of the PDF establish polynomial-time max-flow solution; Appendix E p. 47 gives the explicit vertex-splitting construction for undirected-to-directed and vertex-to-edge cut.
